title: Scotland edge dull Nations Championship Test against Australia
originalTitle: Scotland edge dull Nations Championship Test against Australia
content:
Nations Championship

Scotland (12) 15

Tries: M Fagerson, Dempsey Con: Russell Pens: Russell

Australia (5) 12

Tries: Potter, Jorgensen Con: Donaldson

Scotland edged a dull Nations Championship encounter against Australia at Murrayfield, a game that brought rugby fans crashing back down to earth after the brilliance of France's win against South Africa on Friday and the jaw-dropping wonder of Wales beating the All Blacks on Saturday.

Matt Fagerson, an impressive juggernaut, and Jack Dempsey scored for Scotland, Harry Potter got one for Australia, all in the first half hour.

We waited another 47 minutes before Finn Russell banged over a penalty to make it 15-5. Max Jorgensen's converted try with seconds remaining narrowed the gap. A little flurry at the end of a hugely disappointing, attritional Test.

Apart from isolated moments, it was a game of turnovers, missed opportunities and a terrible absence of anything resembling class. Compliment the grunt, but…

It was chaos. Every breakdown was a lottery, an ugly dogfight. The longer it went on, the more Australia became serial offenders. That game-clinching penalty from Russell was on the back of multiple Wallaby breakdown offences.

There were some seriously creative and pacy players out there but we hardly saw them. Precious little fast ball, precious little buzz from two teams who are well capable of excitement. Neither attack sparked never mind fired. The final whistle came as something of a blessing.

Scotland suffered a blow even before the first whistle when captain Sione Tuipulotu was ruled out with a knee injury. Tom Jordan replaced him in the midfield and Rory Darge took over the leadership role.

Both are stand-up operators, but any Scotland team without Tuipulotu is a weaker outfit.

Huge question marks hung over the pair before the start - Scotland having been blown away by the All Blacks last weekend as the Wallabies went down in flames at Twickenham.

Depending on how it went - Scotland were warm favourites - this was going to be some sort of redemption for one and all sorts of retribution for the other. All of that was in the balance right until the end.

Scotland now move above Wales into fourth in the northern hemisphere table, but their lack of a bonus point on Sunday could cost them. They'll take the win, though.

In the scrappiest encounter, the home side drew first blood. They owned the ball in the early moments, wasted one opportunity to score off a lineout maul, but then struck at the second time of asking.

Finn Russell started it all with a lovely grubber that had Carter Gordon in trouble. It eventually led to a scrum and men over for Scotland. An isolated Fagerson on the right touchline had been calling for it for what must have felt like an age to him. When it did come, he had the easiest job of sliding over.

Russell missed the conversion, but he missed something - or somebody - else just after and it proved costly. One of the many things holding Scotland back is how easy they are to score against - and here was another case for the prosecution.

Rob Valetini and Gordon helped put the Wallabies on the front foot but, when they swept to the left touchline, the whole thing might have come to a halt had Russell made his tackle on Potter. He didn't - and the wing ran on to finish with class.

Scotland thought they'd scored just after but the ball was deemed out of play - a marginal call - when Kyle Steyn mid-air volleyed to Graham, who touched down.

Another injury befell the Scots midway through the opening half when Scott Cummings was replaced by Max Williamson.

The Scots scored their second try soon after. Too much power in the phases and Dempsey drove over against the nation he once represented.

Russell made it 12-5 and it stayed that way despite Billy Pollard being driven over from a lineout maul. The Wallabies were done for obstruction.

The pre-match billing talked about a thrilling try-fest but it was low-key and error-strewn. You expected Scotland to bring their usual ambition but, if anything, they were conservative.

The Wallabies tried to play more rugby, but their game was riddled with mistakes, too. It was chaos out there for large parts of it. Bodies everywhere. A million big hits. Just an awful absence of quality.

Paris on Friday, this was not. Cardiff on Sunday, it was not either.

Pollard got binned for going high on Blair Kinghorn early in the new half but Scotland could do nothing in those precious 10 minutes. They butchered a big opportunity from a close-range lineout - losing their own throw - then won it back and got turned over at the breakdown.

Scotland played much of the second half in Aussie territory but only had those three Russell points to show for it. Just as well.

Australia scored in the last seconds when Jorgensen ran in after a beautiful offload from Jeremy Williams. Ben Donaldson put over the conversion to make it 15-12. Too little, too late for the visitors. Just. Scotland survived.

After two days of Nations Championship rugby that will live long in the memory, this one will have faded in the time it took fans to reach the car park.
